stem: Zubin studies hallway lockers numbered $1$ to $18$. A locker is touched exactly twice when its number has exactly two factors, $1$ and itself.

parts.text: Which claim correctly names only lockers touched exactly twice?

options.text: Lockers $2$, $3$, $5$, $7$, $11$, $13$, and $17$ are touched exactly twice.
Lockers $1$, $2$, $3$, $5$, $7$, and $11$ are touched exactly twice.
Lockers $2$, $4$, $6$, $8$, and $10$ are touched exactly twice.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Exactly two factors means the number is prime. Within $1$ to $18$ the primes are $2$, $3$, $5$, $7$, $11$, $13$, and $17$; locker $1$ has only one factor.

teacher.key_rationale: Touched exactly twice iff prime. Primes in 1..18 are 2,3,5,7,11,13,17. Including 1 or listing evens misses that test.
